Title: How do I change my payment method for my recurring plans/subscriptions?
Content: Payments through a direct DEBIT/CREDIT CARD Log in to your account page. Find your most recent purchase history, and click the edit button next to your card number to change your payment method. Enter a new payment method. Payments through PAYPAL If your plan is with PayPal, they manage your payments. You'll need to change the payment method on PayPal service. Refer to this link. Change your card information by following the link above. Note: When you add a payment method, some payment providers issue a temporary authorization charge. The changes take effect from your next billing date. If your license is not currently active, you can apply your new payment method when you purchase a new license. If your plan is with Alipay, please kindly go to Alipay app and adjust your card information in the subscription page.

Title: UI Changes (Above ver. 11)
Content: Layout Window Workspace Windows / Side Windows Select Mode - Every window can be changed from one to another through the drop-down list at the top center of the window. Duplicate Window - Select a Duplicate icon at the top right-hand corner of a window, and the window will be duplicated as a pop-up. Reset to Default Layout -By toggling the Reset to Default Layout in the bottom right-hand corner, you can bring the window layout back to its original settings. Workspace Windows Set up the number of the Workspace Windows - You can set up the window view options at the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. - As many as four Workspace Window can be shown at one time. - With the shortcut 'Alt+W', you can switch between the current window layout and a full screen of the selected window . (ver. 12.1) Side Windows Close Windows - Only Side windows can be closed, not the Workspace windows. - Select X at the top right-hand corner to close the window. Show/Hide Window - Only Side windows can be either shown and hidden, not the Workspace windows. - Select the arrow on the top left-hand corner to hide the window. Its title will appear as a tab on either side of the screen after being hidden. - If you click on that tab, the window appears again. Arrange Windows - All pop-up windows can be arranged by dragging on either side of the window. Create Windows Tab - Each pop-up window can be dragged onto an existing side window to group them together. - Their title will appear as tabs at the bottom of the window. - You can select a tab to view each window in a group. Toolbar Arrange Toolbar - You can relocate the toolbar to the top, bottom, left, and right of a window by clicking the control handle on the leftmost side Show/Hide Toolbar - Toggle the Show/Hide Toolbar button at the far right of the view icons in each window to make it appear or disappear. Duplicate Tool Group - Move Mouse over a tool group to find sub-tools of the tool group. - A tool group can be duplicated as a pop-up by either clicking the dashed line with scissors in the tool group or by pressing the Enter key. Modular Editor - Modular Editor is added to the tool bar on the 2D window. - You can use the existing Modular Editor, by toggling the Modular Editor icon. Main Menu Duplicate the Menu list - A dash line will be shown if you click a main menu which can be duplicated as a pop-up. - If you either click the dashed line with scissors in a main menu or press the Enter key, the main menu will be duplicated as a pop-up. Open New Window - Main Menu &gt Display &gt Window - Main Menu &gt Window (ver. 12.1) - Follow the indicated path above to open the desired window as a pop up. Environment The Light, Wind, and Camera Controllers icons have been changed. Note - You can restore UI to default by clicking the bottom right icon

Title: What is the Trade-In License?
Content: For enterprise licenses, customers with existing perpetual Enterprise licenses can convert to one copy of a 2-year subscription license per copy of perpetual license by purchasing a subscription conversion. If you have a personal perpetual license and choose to convert it to a subscription license, you can receive one year of subscription per copy of the perpetual license. You can find more information here.

Title: Avatar Measure (above ver 10)
Content: Objective Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement 3D Toolbar Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure Operation Basic/Surface Circumference Measure. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. Click once more when it is in the target shape. A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. Height Measure Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the point to be measured. A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45 tilt. Use Attach to Measure tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure. Attach to Measure (Avatar) Objective Attach avatar tapes to internal or external seam/pattern lines. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement Attach to Measure (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Click and hold down the Edit Measure (Avatar) Attach to Measure (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: In the 3D window, select seam or pattern line to attach to avatar tape. Pattern with the selected line becomes transparent and the selected line gets highlighted in red. Select avatar tape to be attached. Once it is selected, the pattern becomes normal, the attached seam or pattern line and the avatar tape becomes in red. To detach avatar tape from seam or pattern line, click on Attach to Avatar Tape tool again, and press 'Delete' on keyboard. Edit Measure (Avatar) Option Objective Show or hide the length indicated on the Tape Measure Location 3D Toolbar Edit Measure (Avatar) Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the Tape Measure and set the options below. Delete Measure Delete the Tape Measure Duplicate to Symmetric Position (ver 11) Duplicate the tape measure to the symmetrical position of the avatar. Show/ Show All Length The selected tape measure or the length of the entire tape measure is shown or hidden.

Title: Add Arrangement Point
Content: Objective Add new Arrangement Point on the Bound Volume as needed. Note: Without corresponding Bounding Volume, the Arrangement Point is invisible. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Add Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Add A new arrangement point called "Arrangement Point" is now being created at the bottom of the A-Point list in the Arrangement tab, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set details for Arrangement Point. Name Changes the name of the Arrangement Point. Arrangement Arrangement BV Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point to be placed. X Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction The direction in which the Pattern wrapped around the Avatar. Note: Symmetric Arrangement Point Setting Name the Arrangement Point with an underscore and location (R for right and L for left) at the end of the name to set Symmetric Arrangement Point. The name must be the same as the name before the underscore and the alphabet. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default (ver3.0). _R _L Follow the indicated steps below to save the Avatar and Arrangement Points, and reload to apply the setting. Light-blue outer line appears around the Symmetric Arrangement Point. Save Avatar: Main Menu File Save as Avatar Save Arrangement Point: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Save

Title: Select Mesh
Content: Objective Click and drag to select Pattern Mesh freely. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) 3D Toolbar (Click for more than 2 seconds) Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) 3D Toolbar (Click for more than 2 seconds) Select Mesh (Box) / Select Mesh (Lasso) The Garment Mesh is now displayed in green in both the 3D and 2D windows. When using the tool, 3D tools, and Thick Textured Surface are disabled. Click on a vertex (a point of the mesh). The Mesh is now selected. Or click on a desired area on the Garment Click and drag to select the area. The selected area is displayed in green. The selection also appears on the respective 2D Pattern. Click and drag, or use the Gizmo to move the selected Mesh as desired in the 3D window. Note: Click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Shift+Ctrl on the keyboard to select additional mesh. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Ctrl on the keyboard to deselect Mesh from existing selected areas. Select Segment Mesh Double-click on a Pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to select Mesh along the segment. When selecting Mesh on the Pattern in the 2D window, adjacent segment vertices are also selected when the angle difference is less than 20. Select Mesh on the Pattern Double-click on a Pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to select all Mesh on a Pattern. Select Mesh on Internal Line (v4.0.0) Use the same procedure as above to select mesh on specific Internal Lines and Shapes.

Title: Edit AI Bezier Curve
Content: Objective Edit AI Bezier curves with editing tools. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern Operation Edit Curvature Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern Click the point on the AI Bezier Curve to access the handle. When the handle appears, click and drag the point on the desired end of the handle to change the curvature. Note: To edit only one side's curvature, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard while click and dragging the point on the desired end of the handle. (ver MD10) Convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier Curve Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern To convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier curve, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard, and then click and drag the desired Segment Point. Title: OBJ Sequence Export
Content: Objective Export an OBJ Sequence as an OBJ file on every frame of an animation. Exporting a 1 second animation with a 30 fps standard will result in 30 OBJ files being exported. Location Main Menu File Export Animation OBJ Sequence Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Export Animation OBJ Sequence The Save File window opens. Select the desired file and click OK. The Export OBJ Animation window opens. Set below options as needed and click OK. Export OBJ Animation Option Object Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all patterns. You can select specific patterns by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). When utilizing the OBJ (Selected) menu, patterns selected in the 3D and 2D windows are automatically selected and checkbox-ed. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. You can select specific objects by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics and Trims: Select/Deselect all Graphics and Trims. You can select specific Graphics or Trims by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Single Object :Exports the selected object as a single object. If you set the sub-object name, the name of the mesh will be the same with the sub-object name when it is saved. (ver. 5.1.4) You can set it to be saved 'Same as file name' or you can specify 'Object Name'. (ver. 5.1.4) Multiple Objects :Exports the selected object as multiple objects. UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. Image File Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: File Name_0, File Name_1. Texture Size Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Include Internal Shape: Include internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from Unit in file to import is selected. Axis Conversion Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation Entire Area: saves all of the recorded garment animation. Play Area Only: saves only the play area garment animation. Input Frame: Designate and save the frame section. (ver. 5.1.4) You can save the Bone Information for the frame by setting Save with Bone Information (JSON).

Title: Marvelous Designer File Format
Content: Marvelous Designer File Format Type Format Description Garment *.zpac Contains information on Garments, Patterns, Sewing, and Fabrics. Project *.zprj Compresses the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and saves it. The Project file contains the AVT file that has Avatar-related data Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar size, Poses and the ZPac file that contains Garment-related data 3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Material, as well as an animation file if there is animation. Avatar *.avt Contains all the information related to Avatars (Model, Sizing data, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). Pose *.pos Avatar Pose information that, automatically saved whenever the Garment is saved. The Avatars Pose can easily be changed with this file. Avatar Poses from other software can only be saved when the Avatar is a COLLADA file with joints. Joint Motion *.mtn Contains Avatar Motion information. As with the Pose file, can only be saved on COLLADA file Avatars with joint and Animation information. Fabric *.zfab Contains the property values (texture + physical properties) of the set Fabric. Physical Property *.psp Contains the detailed values of Fabric Physical Properties. Topstitch *.sst Contains the type, number of lines, thread thickness, SPI, length, etc. Button *.btn Contains the type, size, and color of Buttons. Buttonhole *.bth Contains the tyle, size, and color of the Buttonholes. Arrangement Point *.arr Arrangement Points are the blue points that are distributed around the Avatar, and are used to arrange Patterns easily around the Avatar. Arrangement Points are created on top of the Arrangement Bounding Volume covering the surroundings of the Avatar. Arrangement Bounding Volume *.pan Arrangement Bounding Volumes are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatars joint. As such, even if the Avatars Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. Camera Projection *.cmp Contains the camera's Field of View information (near, far, etc.). Camera Transformation *.cmt Contains camera view information of the 3D Garment window. Simulation Property *.smp Contains settings for Simulation.

Title: Add Bounding Voulme
Content: Objective Add a Bounding Volume to add arrangement points. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Add Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Add A new Bounding Volume called "Pan" is now being created at the bottom of the Bounding Volume list, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set details for Bounding Volume. Board Check the list of currently added layouts and edit the properties of the layout by selecting the desired item. Name Changes the name of the Bounding Volume. Arrangement BV Joint Name 0 Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume starts. Joint Name 1 Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume ends. Shape (ver MD10) Depending on the shape of the Avatar, the Bounding Volume is set to the Cylinder and Cuboid. Height Sets the height of the Bounding Volume. Length X Adjusts the circumference of the left and right radii of the Bounding Volume. Length Y Adjusts the circumference of the top and bottom radii of the Bounding Volume. Round Corner (ver MD10) It is active only when the Bounding Volume type is set to Cuboid. Adjust the radius of each corner. Hands/Feet If this option is activated, the length of the Bounding Volume is adjusted to the avatar's hands and feet. The moment you click that option, the entire Bounding Volume is refreshed. Note: If the order below/above the joint points is reversed, the left and right sides are flipped when arranging the Pattern.
